title: Minimum Operations to Reach Target Array
summary: Given two integer arrays nums and target of equal length, you can perform operations to make nums match target.
statement: Given two integer arrays nums and target of equal length, you can perform operations to make nums match target. An operation consists of selecting an integer x, identifying maximal contiguous segments of nums where all elements are x, and simultaneously updating these segments to match the corresponding values in target. The task is to determine the least number of such operations needed.
constraints: nums and target have equal length.
One operation chooses a current value x and updates all mismatched occurrences selected by its maximal equal-value segments to their target values.
Return the least operations needed to make nums equal target.
reference_solution:
def minimum_target_array_operations(nums,target):
    return len({value for value,wanted in zip(nums,target) if value!=wanted})
hints: An operation is keyed by the original value it selects.
Correct positions require no work; among mismatches, all equal original values can be handled together.
Collect nums[i] where nums[i]!=target[i] and return the set size.
Each distinct mismatched source value needs one operation and one operation suffices for all of its segments.
editorial: Each distinct mismatched source value needs one operation and one operation suffices for all of its segments.

tests.explanation: The mismatches have original values one and two, requiring two operations.
Both mismatches share original value one, so one operation updates them together.
